facts: A real manufacturing project required two domestic-platform servers, SCADA/historian, OT networking, UPS, displays and implementation services.
The design source included an equipment schedule, a physical connection diagram, a converted workshop plan and several prior budget versions.
The project required remote start/stop of a utility subsystem while keeping PLC interlocks authoritative.
findings: The approximately 18 percent revision was mainly caused by under-scoped SCADA licensing, display installation, industrial switching and backup—not by server price alone.
Public partial server configurations were too weak to justify reducing the saved configured-server baseline.
Separating Runtime, Development, I/O points, Web, historian, alarm, API and drivers exposed a material software-budget gap.
A nominal UPS VA label was insufficient until W rating, runtime curve and shutdown integration were checked.
rule_changes: Preserve existing configurable-enterprise prices unless stronger current evidence passes the revision gate.
Break SCADA licensing into independently quoted components.
Require explicit OT remote-control FAT/SAT tests and positive equipment feedback.
limitations: The revised amount is a design-stage budget, not an awarded or settled contract value.
Supplier quotations and final implementation quantities were still pending, so this case does not measure final forecast accuracy.
Budget values are rounded to the nearest CNY 10000; customer, supplier and location identifiers are removed.
